decisions.reason: Although the citrus harvesting crate builds on the firm's reusable-crate know-how, its crop-specific niche and two years without visible market presence suggest limited commercial learning and a likely reallocation of resources to broader packaging platforms.

The foldable large container is highly related to the firm's core container capabilities, but prolonged non-observation after launch points to weak distinct traction or absorption into the standard range, making withdrawal of the launched line slightly more likely than retention.

A medium-duty rackable pallet fits existing pallet expertise well, yet the lack of visible follow-through indicates that management would likely rationalize this line in favor of stronger or more established pallet offerings.

The spill-retention pallet is adjacent rather than central to the firm's main reusable transport-packaging franchise, and sustained absence from the market signal makes it the clearest candidate for exit and resource redeployment.

This pallet with load retainers draws on familiar platform knowledge, but as a narrower variant with no continued visibility it is more likely to be discontinued as a standalone product than actively developed further.
